step: R11 investigation -- what should the TD-5 write-back gate key on (design docs/designs/textdecode-policy-v2-2026-08-22.md section 18.1/18.4, open question 6)
harness: rust/crates/runtime/src/textdecode/r11_gate_probe.rs (cargo test, always-run, no env gate, small deterministic corpus)
reproduction: cd rust && cargo test -p agentry-runtime --release textdecode::r11_gate_probe -- --nocapture

1_bomPinnedOnly.status: not re-measured here -- design section 18.1 already confirms this is TD-2's actual current behavior; free, insufficient alone for R11's legacy-multi-byte population

2_detectedEncodingChangedVsCached.status: not re-measured here -- design section 18.1 already argues this is a supplementary signal only, fires on second read of an already-cached path, not first open

3_highBitByteDensityHeuristic.source: design section 18.1 candidate 3, made concrete and measured by this investigation

measured.finding: a naive density greater than 0.5 threshold flags every measured lossy case AND the genuine, clean, all-Cyrillic control -- the two populations are not density-separable in this corpus. Confirms section 18.1 candidate 3's own named false-positive risk empirically, not just theoretically.

4_roundTripReencodeOracle.source: named explicitly by the task, not evaluated in section 18.1

corpus: truncated-shift-jis (R11 core case, matches design section 18.1's own tests.rs 532-551 construction)
measured.mechanism: every case above reclassifies to a single-byte legacy label (windows-1252 x5, GBK x1) whose encoding_rs decode/encode pair is a total, injective byte-scalar mapping over all 256 byte values -- re-encoding the (wrong, garbled) decoded text via the (wrong) detected label reproduces the original raw bytes exactly, so the oracle reports every case as clean.
measured.falsePositiveCheck: 0/1 -- correctly reports the clean windows-1252 control as clean
measured.costNote: single-sample measurement (137-byte Shift-JIS buffer, 5000 iterations release profile): decode-only about 5.1-7.4us per call, decode+reencode about 6.0-8.8us per call (variance between runs is environmental, not corpus-dependent). A second full pass over the buffer, roughly 16-19 percent wall-time overhead at this size for the Legacy-label subset only (BOM-pinned UTF-16/UTF-32 cases do not need it -- had_replacements already covers them).

4_roundTripReencodeOracle.verdict: FALSE NEGATIVE for R11's core population. Not a partial-coverage gap -- 0 percent recall on every constructed corruption shape (truncation, mid-sequence, cross-encoding splice) across every legacy multi-byte candidate tested.

5_windows1252C1GapByteSignal.source: novel, proposed by this investigation as a narrower alternative to density
5_windows1252C1GapByteSignal.description: the 5 WHATWG windows-1252 gap bytes (0x81, 0x8D, 0x8F, 0x90, 0x9D) map to C1 control scalars rather than erroring (design section 10 R5, section 18.1) -- genuine natural-language windows-1252 text essentially never contains them (no printable glyph was ever assigned). Their presence in Legacy(WINDOWS_1252)-labeled decoded text is a candidate discriminator.

measured.recallOnWindows1252LabeledLossySubset: 2/5 (40 percent) -- of the 5 lossy cases that specifically reclassify to windows-1252 (the GBK-labeled splice case is out of this narrow signal's scope by construction)
measured.falsePositiveCheck: 0/3 (strengthened from an initial n=1 check after adversarial review) -- three deliberately varied clean windows-1252 controls, including two constructed specifically to be dense in the legitimately-assigned 0x80-0x9F printable range (curly quotes, dashes, bullet, trademark, dagger, per-mille, angle quotes, Scaron/Zcaron/OE), none contain a gap byte. n=3 is still small; this is 'no false positive found under adversarial construction', not a proof of zero false-positive rate.

5_windows1252C1GapByteSignal.verdict: Zero measured false positives across 3 adversarially-varied clean controls (up from 1), but incomplete recall (40 percent on its own applicable subset) and inapplicable to non-windows-1252 reclassification targets (the measured GBK case). NOT recommended as a hard/binding write-back gate at this evidence level (n=3 false-positive testing is not sufficient basis to block a user's save) -- recommended, if used at all, as a non-blocking supplementary/advisory signal only. See section 18.4 for the full recommendation.

recallByCandidate.densityHeuristicAlone: 100 percent recall but also 100 percent false-positive on the hostile clean control -- not usable as a hard gate
recallByCandidate.c1GapByteSignal: 40 percent on its applicable subset, 0/3 false positive (adversarially strengthened, still small-n)

summary.conclusion: No single cheap signal measured here closes R11 for the legacy-multi-byte single-byte-fallback-reclassification population without either missing it entirely (round-trip), risking blocking legitimate dense non-Latin-script content (density alone), or resting on too small an evidence base to justify a hard gate (C1-gap-byte signal, n=3 false-positive testing). See section 18.4 for the composite recommendation: the disclosed accept-the-residual-risk path carries the recommendation, with the gap-byte signal available only as a non-blocking advisory addition, not a binding TD-5 done-when criterion.
